voci.titolo: NYC Can Proceed With Pied-a-Terre Tax as Court Weighs Appeal
voci.riassunto: New York City can proceed with the rollout of its pied-à-terre tax while an appeals court considers a legal challenge.

voci.titolo: These 5 chip stocks are cheaper than the S&P 500 — and offer faster growth
voci.riassunto: Micron and Nvidia are among high-profile semiconductor companies that have been raking in cash and still have inexpensive stocks.

voci.titolo: Trade deficit hits $105.6 billion, widest since just before Trump tariffs enacted last year
voci.riassunto: That marked a 13.7% jump from July and was ahead of the Dow Jones consensus estimate for $102 billion.

voci.titolo: Man Group Disputes View That High Inflation Is Bad for Bonds
voci.riassunto: High inflation alone isn’t bad for US Treasuries — instead, it’s a rapid increase in the pace of price growth that does the most damage, according to a study by Man Group.

voci.titolo: Emerging-Market Assets Extend Gains as US Yields Decline
voci.riassunto: Emerging-market assets extended their gains as a combination of lower US bond yields, a weaker dollar and relatively steady oil prices provide relief to global markets.

voci.titolo: US Treasuries Yields Fall From 2002 High as Oil Prices Dip
voci.riassunto: US bond yields fell from their highest levels since 2002 as oil prices stabilized and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent insisted the government’s debt load can be tamed.

voci.titolo: World Bank warns of AI concentration risks as it lifts East Asia and Pacific growth outlook to 4.5%
voci.riassunto: The World Bank now expects the region to grow 4.5% this year, but flagged that trade growth outside AI-related goods has been "weak or negative."

voci.titolo: The 2029 tipping point: Western populations are about to start shrinking, piling pressure on public finances
voci.riassunto: Moody's predicts that the world's aging populations will have fundamental impacts on the global economy and lead to difficult policy decisions.

voci.titolo: Men are losing ground in the labor market. Here's why
